title: Worst-case dynamic Courcelle theorem at bounded treewidth
formal: Under edge updates preserving treewidth at most \(k\), can every fixed counting monadic second-order graph property be maintained in \(f(k,\varphi)\operatorname{polylog}n\) worst-case update time?
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Specify CMSO with edge-set quantification, the update promise, initialization, query time and the distinction from known amortized bounds.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence or universal proposition, or of its logical negation. This is a provisional candidate, not a completed benchmark specification. Pending: Specify CMSO with edge-set quantification, the update promise, initialization, query time and the distinction from known amortized bounds.
context: The supplied catalogue associates this question with Michal Pilipczuk. This is an editorial research connection, not a claim of authorship or a personal research agenda. The candidate retains the bibliography and dated caveats from that catalogue; these have not received a comprehensive independent literature review.
why: A worst-case dynamic Courcelle theorem would make logical tractability stable under every individual update.

import_provenance.original_title: Worst-case dynamic Courcelle theorem at bounded treewidth
import_provenance.original_statement: Under edge insertions and deletions preserving treewidth at most k, can every fixed CMSO₂ graph property be maintained in f(k,φ)·polylog(n) worst-case update time? This is an editorial strengthening of Pilipczuk and coauthors’ dynamic decomposition and logical-property data structures.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The amortized polylogarithmic target was already resolved in 2025; the question specifically asks for a worst-case bound.
